items.recapEn: Rain caught Hana and Ken in the Goyu pine avenue. Murakami-san’s hatago no longer takes guests, but she waved them in: floorboards creaking, kettle whistling, rain drumming the roof. Travellers’ names and poems are carved on the pillars. Not only rain but wind came, so Ken made miso soup and they agreed to eat at Akasaka, one pine avenue away.

items.recapEn: By Murakami-san’s fire Hana was not only starving but cold; Ken’s answer was ‘then eat’, and she slurped a second bowl. His noodle count reached eighty-two. Hana asked to write on the pillars; Murakami-san said the old travellers were forgiven, not today’s, and gave her a notebook instead, then lent two umbrellas to pass on to someone else.
